newsitem.title: MALAWI: Court finds Malawi's Banda too old to stand trial.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Malawi's Banda too old to stand trial.

text.p: A Malawi High Court on Tuesday found former "life president" Kamuzu Banda too old and ill to stand trial on charges of fraud involving $9 million.

National radio quoted Judge Duncan Tambala as saying that Banda, believed to be 96, was too old to appear in court. The court could not try Banda in his absence as it would violate his constitutional right to a fair trial, the judge added.
Tambala said however if Banda's condition improved the state could again press charges.
Banda, who ruled Malawi with an iron first for three decades, was not present in court on Tuesday.
He was charged together with three senior members of his opposition Malawi Congress Party for allegedly using public funds to build a grammar school, the Kamuzu Academy.
The three other accused, including Banda's long-time companion Cecilia Kadzamira, his former confidant John Tembo and former finance minister Louis Chimango, have pleaded not guilty to the charges.
Banda was prime minister when Malawi gained its independence from Britain in 1964, became president in 1966 and proclaimed himself president for life in 1971, crushing all dissent.
His grip on power however slipped when he lost the presidency to a former protege, Bakili Muluzi, during democratic elections in 1994.
